title: Debt Defense Rules — Schema v1.0
description: Schema for the Civil Justice as Code debt-defense rules library. Extends the eviction-line format (docs/SCHEMA_V2_DESIGN_SPEC.md) rather than replacing it, per DEBT_PROJECT_ARCHITECTURE_SPEC.md §2. Key structural difference from the eviction schema: tier is a NODE property, not a FILE property — a single release can ship federal-spine nodes at VALIDATED alongside a newly-added state's garnishment table at CORROBORATED. Copyright 2026 Andrew M Cohen. Apache 2.0.

_copyright.description: Copyright notice. Must be: 'Copyright 2026 Andrew M Cohen. Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0.'

schema_version.description: Schema version identifier. Must be exactly 'debt-v1'.

scope.description: Jurisdiction resolution as a first-class input (spec §2) — resolved once, early, not per-node the way the eviction line resolves per-file.

level.description: federal = one jurisdiction-agnostic file amortizing across all 50 states + DC (FDCPA/Reg F/FCRA spine); state = per-state layer (SOL, deadlines, exemptions, service/default-judgment procedure).

jurisdiction.description: For level=federal, state/state_name are null (applies everywhere federal law reaches).

state.description: Two-letter postal abbreviation (e.g., TX) or DC; null for federal-level files

model.description: AI model used for generation, e.g. claude-sonnet-4-6

statutory_sources.description: All statutes/regulations cited across all nodes in this file

nodes.description: The unit of encoding. Each node carries its own tier, band, sourcing, completeness checklist, and consequences — per spec §2, tier and band are node properties, not file properties.

band.description: Per docs/GLOSSARY.md and CJAC_ROADMAP.md, reconciled in spec §2: 1 = deterministic/freezable outcome (e.g., SOL determination); 2 = structured-subjective (e.g., chain-of-title adequacy — lookup-able structure, judgment application); 3 = genuinely discretionary, boundary-marker only, never a target to cross (e.g., settle-vs-fight, bankruptcy-referral).

tier.description: Per spec §4 tier-promotion rules. DRAFT -> CORROBORATED: passes grounded-corroboration/adversarial/mutation-testing/disagreement-queue stages (§3a-d) with no unresolved disagreement. CORROBORATED -> VALIDATED: survives the statistical sampling audit (§3e) at attorney certification (§3g). Demotion triggers: statute/case-watch hit, audit failure, or a mutation-testing miss.

grounded_derivation.description: Per spec §3(a): a model that answers correctly but can't point to the specific statutory/regulatory text it derived the answer from does not count.

quoted_text.description: Verbatim source text the derivation rests on.

citation_verified.description: Mechanically verified against live source text, per §3(a).

logic.description: The rule content itself. Deliberately unstructured beyond this point in v1 — first nodes will establish the concrete shape; do not over-specify before real content exists (see CLAUDE.md posture on schema-before-content).

completeness_checklist.description: Per spec §2: drives the guided-interview / voice-demo elicitation layer (§5) and is scored directly by the Direction E Tier 2 harness's elicitation-coverage metric.

fact.description: Plain-language description of the fact needed.

dispositive.description: Whether this fact changes the outcome (vs. merely contextual).

consequences_and_next_steps.description: Per spec §2: never a bare classification — structurally required, not prose. What to file, by when.

ratification.description: Per spec §3(g): a named attorney certifies the RELEASE based on aggregate pipeline evidence, not a node-by-node signoff. This block records which release certification this node last cleared under, not a per-node attorney signature.

disagreement_flags.description: Per spec §3(d): model-vs-model or model-vs-source conflicts, auto-filed with evidence attached.
